paragraphs: Here's what I love about this prayer, friend. It holds nothing back. The people lay out the hunger, the hurt and the grief right in front of the LORD, one thing at a time. They don't clean it up first, and they don't wait until they feel better. They just say, "Remember, O LORD, what has happened to us" (Lamentations 5:1).

Now look at the turn. Right in the middle of all that pain, the prayer says, "You, O LORD, reign forever; Your throne endures from generation to generation" (Lamentations 5:19). And then, in the very next breath, it asks, "Why have You forgotten us forever?" (Lamentations 5:20). Both things are in the same prayer. So you can believe the LORD is on His throne and still bring Him your hardest question, and He lets you do both.

The prayer also owns its part: "Woe to us, for we have sinned!" (Lamentations 5:16). Then it asks the LORD, "Restore us to Yourself, O LORD, so we may return; renew our days as of old" (Lamentations 5:21). The big ask is to be brought back to HIM. Friend, I know what it is to be worn out and tucked in the dark, and I know what it is to be made new. So when you're hurting, bring it all to the LORD, the ache, the questions and even the fear at the end. He's the one worth bringing it to.
